title: Redwood Console: Tracing + Request Logs Debugging Demo

transcript:
Header: 2026-07-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Marco Li (Redwood Product), Sara Thompson (Nebula VP ML), Daniel Ruiz (Nebula SRE), Maya Patel (Nebula Security)

Summary: Quick demo of console traces -> error analysis -> request logs. Showed an example KV-cache miss investigation and how to attach a request payload export. Discussed compliance and POC next steps.

00:00 Alex Chen: All right good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, i think we have Priya and Marco with me as well. can you hear us ok?
00:06 Sara Thompson: Yep we're good, thanks. we've been poking at the hosted api for a bit but we hit a couple of production errors and wanted to see the debugging flow.
00:12 Alex Chen: Perfect that's what today's for. quick agenda: tracing overview, error analysis, request logs, and then Q&A. Priya will do the live console demo.
01:04 Priya Kumar: Ok jumping in — this is the tracing UI, it's a top-down view that groups requests by route and by model version. you'll see an example trace here where we have a 503 on generation. note that the timestamps are rough, the console sometimes shows relative times.
01:38 Daniel Ruiz: Quick question — can I filter traces by customer id or api key? we have multiple product lines.
01:45 Priya Kumar: Yes you can filter by api key, customer id, or route. i'll show the filter panel in a sec. also note we collect per-token latency, so you can see where the slowdown spikes (eg initial attn, kv-cache fill).
02:22 Mara Li: sorry marco — marco li: one thing to call out — the trace links down to request logs and you can open the raw payload, or export. i'll demo that.
03:01 Sara Thompson: sometimes i see "K-V cash" misses in our monitoring, is that the same as KV cache?
03:08 Priya Kumar: yes, that's kv-cache, sometimes transcribers write it weird. a miss shows up as 'cache miss' in the trace timeline.
04:15 Priya Kumar: here's a trace with a large decoder latency. see at 00:12 there's a big jump — if we click into the span it shows model->runtime kernel stall and a note about quantization fallback.
05:02 Daniel Ruiz: hmm quantization fallback — do you mean it automatically falls back to fp16 when a kernel isn't available? we've seen spikes when switching quantized variants.
05:12 Priya Kumar: in some cases the runtime will pick a different kernel path, yes, it can cause a latency bump. you can pin model variants per-route to avoid surprises.
06:00 Maya Patel: security question — how long do you keep request logs and are they redacted for pii?
06:10 Priya Kumar: default retention is 30 days in hosted, but for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention. redaction: request-level PII redaction is configurable and we also have integrations with customer KMS for payload encryption at rest. i'll attach the security docs after.
07:00 Alex Chen: demoing error analysis now — you can group by error code, by model, or by customer. here i'm grouping by error signature so you can see a regression trend.
07:30 Priya Kumar: i'll open a sample error trace — notice the stack of spans: api proxy -> routing -> runtime -> model. the runtime span has metadata about token sequence length and kv cache hits. see here it says "kv_cache_hit: false" for the failing requests.
08:10 Daniel Ruiz: what causes cache misses? we preface with a user prompt that should be long-lived prefix.
08:20 Priya Kumar: misses happen when the prefix isn't identical (even whitespace), or when you have different session ids. we also surface prefix clustering to show similar keys so you can tune your caching strategy.
09:05 Sara Thompson: can you show me how to jump from the trace to the raw request log?
09:12 Priya Kumar: sure i click the request id link, it opens the request log panel, you can see headers, body, model_id, token counts, and the full stack traces for the runtime error.
10:01 Priya Kumar: note the request log shows inference metadata and a pointer to the binary request payload if you need it. for compliance we can mask or redact the payload on export.
11:20 Alex Chen: now i'll show alerting — you can create alerts on error rate, percentiles, or specific error signatures. these tie into slack, pagerduty, or a webhook.
12:05 Daniel Ruiz: can alerts be per-route? we want only high-priority routes to page our on-call.
12:12 Alex Chen: yes alerts are per-route or per-model. you can have multi-channel escalation and auto-snooze rules.
13:00 Priya Kumar: demoing request log search — you can search by request id, trace id, model version, error code, or free text in the request body (if redaction isn't enabled). the full text search is indexed for the last N days depending on retention.
14:10 Sara Thompson: we have a compliance requirement for logs to be stored in our VPC. how does Private deployment handle that?
14:20 Marco Li: for Private deployments we run a control plane locally or in your VPC and you can configure log sinks to S3-compatible storage in your account. we also support on-prem air-gapped installs with a support plan.
15:05 Maya Patel: do you have SOC2 docs?
15:10 Alex Chen: yes SOC2 type 2, ISO and penetration test summaries — i'll send the pack. these are in the security docs link.
16:00 Priya Kumar: back to debugging flow — here's a typical triage: identify the error signature in error analysis -> open a representative trace -> go to request log -> inspect payload and runtime spans -> if needed ask for a full payload export to reproduce locally.
17:30 Daniel Ruiz: the team wants to run a latency + cost benchmark; can you run sample runs with our model and token distribution?
17:45 Alex Chen: we can run benchmarks as part of a POC. we normally ask for a sample corpus and a workload profile. for Dedicated we can also show pricing tradeoffs for batch sizes and quantization settings.
19:10 Priya Kumar: i'll show an example using request logs to find high-cost paths: filter by tokens per request and cost per request, then group by route. you can quickly see 90th percentile token usage.
20:00 Sara Thompson: earlier you mentioned quantization regression detection — how do you surface quality changes?
20:12 Marco Li: Redwood Optimize ties into the console — we keep eval sets and can run regressions when a model or quantization profile changes. alerts can be triggered when eval metrics drop beyond a threshold.
21:30 Daniel Ruiz: slightly off-topic — do you support private key management for model weights?
21:40 Alex Chen: weights are not customer-managed in hosted, but in Private you can host model binaries in your environment and manage keys via KMS/HSM. we'll scope that in the POC.
22:50 Priya Kumar: back to the concrete debugging example — i opened a request with a failure and exported the payload. see the payload: user prompt + context, but notice we had an unexpected newline that changed the prefix key so it missed the kv cache. simple fix in client side to normalize whitespace.
24:05 Sara Thompson: oh that makes sense, some of our SDKs strip trailing spaces differently.
24:30 Priya Kumar: yes those subtle differences cause cache key divergence. the console help page has a small snippet for normalizing prompts.
25:20 Alex Chen: quick pause for any questions?
25:35 Maya Patel: about redaction: if we enable automatic PII redaction, can we still export request payloads for debugging?
25:45 Priya Kumar: yes, but exports will be masked by default; we can provide a secure workflow where a customer-approved engineer decrypts or requests an unmasked export if the customer allows it. this is part of the security playbook.
27:00 Daniel Ruiz: can the request logs be forwarded to our splunk/elastic? we want to centralize.
27:12 Marco Li: yes we have log sinks and native integrations for Splunk/Elastic/Kinesis. you can route selectively by route or error level.
28:30 Priya Kumar: switching to timeline — here's a regression example where a model rollout increased error rate. we used the trace then request logs to find the offending prompt pattern, rolled back, and opened an incident.
30:00 Sara Thompson: for the POC we want to reproduce a few of our high-latency cases and measure cost delta if we enable batching or quantize. what's the minimum dedicated footprint?
30:15 Alex Chen: minimum depends on model size; for 7B we'd typically start with a single GPU pod for evaluation, for 30B you'd need 2+ GPUs. we'll propose options in the worksheet.
31:50 Priya Kumar: demoed the request replay feature — you can replay a request against a model variant in a sandbox to compare latency and outputs without impacting production.
33:12 Daniel Ruiz: does replay use real user data? is that allowed?
33:20 Priya Kumar: replay respects redaction rules; by default payloads are masked, but for POC we can enable unmasked replay within a secure sandbox in the customer's VPC for debugging under NDA.
34:40 Alex Chen: note for Dedicated we provide per-token cost breakdowns in the console and token-level attribution down to the request id.
35:50 Sara Thompson: are there SDKs for programmatic access to traces and request logs? we want to integrate with our internal dashboards.
36:00 Marco Li: yes, REST endpoints and a python sdk. we also export to open telemetry in some enterprise plans.
37:20 Priya Kumar: small demo: i search for a request id you shared earlier -> shows request body, runtime spans, and a binary pointer. you can click "open in replay" and run against older model versions.
38:15 Daniel Ruiz: one more question — what is your typical turnaround for debugging a failing request?
38:22 Alex Chen: for POC partners we offer a dedicated SE for triage with a 24-48h initial turnaround. for enterprise support SLAs are defined in the contract.
39:55 Maya Patel: are audit logs available? our auditors need access to admin actions.
40:05 Alex Chen: yes admin/audit logs for console actions, token changes, and rollouts; these can be ingested to your SIEM.
41:30 Priya Kumar: wrapping up the demo — i'll attach the exact queries we used for the trace -> request log pivots and a small checklist for reproducing issues locally.
42:05 Alex Chen: recap: we'll send pricing/worksheet, security docs, and tracing guide. Priya will share queries and Marco will scope the replay and benchmark steps. customer to provide failing request ids.
42:30 Sara Thompson: thanks this was helpful, i'll sync with infra and security and get the IDs.
43:00 Alex Chen: great, we'll follow up with links and the recording. any final Qs?
43:12 Daniel Ruiz: none from me, thanks.
43:15 Maya Patel: thanks all.
43:30 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, talk soon.

Attachments / Links referenced: https://redwood.dev/docs/tracing-guide (tracing guide), https://redwood.dev/security/soc2.pdf (security pack), shared worksheet: https://sheets.redwood.com/nebulapoctemplate (Dedicated pricing worksheet)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-typed acronyms (K-V cash -> KV cache), speaker labels sometimes shortened.
